meta.title: Speech Recognition with Whisper
meta.thesis: Speech Recognition with Whisper is practical when learners can apply it to this concrete case: A sales team transcribes calls with Whisper and needs timestamps, speaker checks, and privacy handling. By the end, they should be able to build or review speech-to-text transcription QA plan, measure word error rate on domain vocabulary, and catch the failure where names and product terms are confidently mistranscribed.

mentalMap.title: Speech Recognition with Whisper: mental map
mentalMap.caption: Use Whisper-style ASR by preparing audio, transcribing, checking timestamps and domain terms, measuring quality, and gating downstream use.
mentalMap.oneLineThesis: Speech recognition is useful when transcripts become verified data, not when raw audio is blindly treated as truth.

objectives: Anchor in a spoken learner question.

blocks.title: A transcript is an interpretation of audio

spans.text: Problem anchor: a learner asks a spoken question about backpropagation. The app wants to transcribe it, retrieve lesson notes, and answer. Whisper is a general-purpose speech recognition model, but output still needs checks for noise, accents, names, equations, and domain terms.

blocks.analogy: ASR is a careful listener with a keyboard, not an audio truth oracle.

spans.text: Audio ID: learner-q-104.wav. Expected terms: gradient, loss, derivative. Transcript: "Why does the gradient get smaller in earlier layers?" Review notes: correct terms, no overlap, approved for retrieval.

blocks.title: Transcript trust
blocks.prompt: Why review transcripts before agent use?

options.text: ASR can produce fluent but wrong text for noisy, accented, or technical audio.
Audio transcripts never affect downstream behavior.

blocks.explanation: Agents and retrieval inherit transcript errors.

modules.title: Audio preparation changes transcription quality
modules.sub: Garbage audio makes confident text unreliable.
modules.summary: Before decoding, inspect format, clipping, background noise, and segmentation.

blocks.title: The model hears what the pipeline gives it

spans.text: Background music, clipping, long silence, overlapping speakers, and bad segmentation can change ASR output. Store audio metadata, normalize format, chunk long files, and preserve timestamps so reviewers can jump back to source audio.

modules.title: Timestamps make correction possible
modules.sub: Language, task, and segment boundaries matter downstream.
modules.summary: The ASR result should carry model, language, timestamps, and review metadata.

spans.text: For a lesson product, store whether the task was transcription or translation, the model/version, language, segment timestamps, and reviewer status. A plain text blob is not enough for correction or audit.
Segment 00:12-00:17 says "back probation" instead of "backpropagation." The reviewer clicks the timestamp, hears the audio, corrects the term, and marks the transcript approved for retrieval.

modules.title: Code a transcript quality gate
modules.sub: Check domain terms before transcripts feed search.
modules.summary: A small QA script catches missing terms and routes unreviewed transcripts to review.

blocks.title: Transcript QA before retrieval indexing
blocks.code:
transcript = {
    "audio_id": "learner-q-104.wav",
    "model": "whisper-large-v3",
    "language": "en",
    "segments": [{"start": 0.0, "end": 4.2, "text": "Why does the gradient get smaller in earlier layers?"}],
    "reviewed": False,
}
required_terms = {"gradient", "layers"}
text = " ".join(seg["text"].lower() for seg in transcript["segments"])
missing_terms = sorted(term for term in required_terms if term not in text)
needs_review = bool(missing_terms) or not transcript["reviewed"]
print({"missing_terms": missing_terms, "needs_review": needs_review})

spans.text: This is a product gate: if important terms are missing or the transcript is unreviewed, do not treat it as trusted retrieval text.

predictThenReveal.prompt: What prints when reviewed is False but all required terms are present?
predictThenReveal.answer: missing_terms is empty, but needs_review is true because review approval is still missing.

spans.text: Checklist: audio metadata stored; model/language/task recorded; timestamps preserved; long audio chunked; technical terms reviewed; transcript status controls downstream search or agent use.

modules.title: Transcripts feed agents only after approval
modules.summary: ASR output becomes safer when treated as evidence with correction and rollback.

blocks.title: A transcript can become a retrieval bug

spans.text: Once transcribed, audio may enter search, summaries, tools, or memory. Misheard words can retrieve the wrong lesson. Spoken malicious instructions can become text an agent sees. Keep transcript provenance, user intent, and approval status attached.

blocks.ruleOfThumb: Index transcripts only when quality, timestamps, and review status match downstream risk.
blocks.useWhen: Use ASR for captions, searchable lessons, spoken questions, and agent inputs when correction is possible.
blocks.avoidWhen: Avoid high-impact automation from raw transcripts without review, confidence checks, and audit trails.

diffusion.label: Diffusion
diffusion.laymanDefinition: A generative process that learns to turn noise into structured media.
diffusion.technicalNote: Diffusion systems combine denoising steps, conditioning, schedulers, and safety controls; quality and provenance depend on the full pipeline.

latent_space.label: Latent space
latent_space.laymanDefinition: A compressed representation where models manipulate meaning more efficiently than raw pixels or audio.
latent_space.technicalNote: Latent-space choices affect speed, detail, editability, artifacts, and what safety or provenance checks can inspect.

pipeline.label: Pipeline
pipeline.laymanDefinition: The ordered set of model, preprocessing, generation, postprocessing, and safety steps.
pipeline.technicalNote: Media pipelines should pin model versions, prompts, parameters, assets, moderation, watermarking, and review metadata for reproducibility.

vlm.label: VLM
vlm.laymanDefinition: A model that connects visual inputs with language understanding or generation.
vlm.technicalNote: VLM workflows need image preprocessing, prompt grounding, output validation, and privacy review for uploaded visual content.

asr.label: ASR
asr.laymanDefinition: Technology that converts spoken audio into text.
asr.technicalNote: ASR systems should track language, accent, noise, timestamps, confidence, privacy, and downstream correction paths.

provenance.label: Provenance
provenance.laymanDefinition: Evidence about where media came from and how it was created or edited.
provenance.technicalNote: Provenance for generated media includes source assets, model versions, prompts, parameters, edits, disclosures, and review decisions.
